advice: Hypothesis, unverified: replace the generated path’s full 512×512 temporary A transpose with bounded, per-call packing of A panels sized for one output-row block and a small K block. In the wrapper’s 512 path, allocate a reusable scratch panel inside gemm, pack each A block from row-major A into the contiguous K-by-row layout consumed by the existing SME2 loads, and run the matching output-row block before reusing the panel. Keep B in its current layout. Handle the last row and K blocks with bounded copies and the existing general-size fallback; free scratch before gemm returns. This targets less temporary traffic and better A-panel reuse, but may lose if repeated packing or the altered block schedule costs more than the removed transpose.
risks: The existing reference assembly has fixed addressing and consumes the full generated transpose layout; panel packing needs a correspondingly bounded compute path or carefully adapted load/block addressing. Incorrect offsets can mix panels or write outside C. Allocation failure must preserve correct behavior. Packing, allocation, all panel work, and cleanup remain inside the timed call, so a kernel-only gain may disappear end to end. This is a proposal, not a measured result.
